statement: Merkle membership of SHA-256('avpn/member/v1'||s) in a tree of 2^20 commitments, and nullifier SHA-256('avpn/nullifier/v1'||s||epoch||scope); public: root, epoch, scope, nullifier
machine: Intel Core i7-8565U (2018 laptop, 4 cores / 8 threads), 15 GiB RAM, CPU proving only (no GPU)
checks: distinct members: distinct nullifiers, same root
outsider cannot produce the members' root
journal carries neither the secret nor the leaf
zkvm: risc0-zkvm 3.1 (STARK over BabyBear, FRI; succinct receipt, no SNARK wrapper)
notes: Real proofs: the host refuses RISC0_DEV_MODE (which fakes them) and asserts a succinct receipt.
prove_seconds is the first of six proofs; the run's six took 695 s in all, about 2 minutes each.
The succinct receipt is one STARK (hash-based, post-quantum). RISC Zero's Groth16 wrapper would shrink it to a few hundred bytes but rests on elliptic curves, so it is not used.
